evidence: src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) and this.prisma.stockCount.create(...) / findMany() use the raw ORM client, while ReceivingService uses the ItemTable and BinTable gateways.
src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: never uses Bin, Item or StockError. count(binCode, counted, expected) takes `expected` from the caller instead of reading the bin's quantity from Bin.
src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: the discrepancy rule `counted - expected` (and the counted !== expected check) is written out separately in count() and in openDiscrepancies().
src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts: pick() has `new Bin(data.code, data.sku, data.quantity, data.maxWeightGrams)`, which repeats the row-to-Bin mapping in the private bin(code) helper.

src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts: receive() and pick() load data through ItemTable/BinTable and apply the rules through Bin.put/Bin.take/Item.needsReorder, which is the abstraction CycleCountService does not use.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services deal with warehouse stock, so their concern is broadly cohesive. They do not use the same abstraction, though. ReceivingService gets data through the BinTable and ItemTable gateways and works on Bin, Item and StockError from business/stock, so the bin and item rules stay in those classes. CycleCountService skips all of that. It uses the raw PrismaService client (prisma.stockCount.create/findMany), works on raw rows, takes `expected` from the caller instead of reading the bin's quantity from Bin, and returns a separate Discrepancy shape. That bypasses the stock model the module otherwise builds on. It also repeats a rule inside its own file: `counted - expected` and the counted/expected comparison appear in both count() and openDiscrepancies(). In ReceivingService, pick() rebuilds Bin inline with `new Bin(data.code, data.sku, data.quantity, data.maxWeightGrams)`, copying the mapping already in the private bin() helper. These inconsistencies fail the rubric. Import direction itself is not judged here.

Writes the discrepancy rule (counted !== expected, delta = counted - expected) separately in count() and openDiscrepancies() instead of keeping it in one place.
pick() builds Bin inline (new Bin(data.code, data.sku, data.quantity, data.maxWeightGrams)), repeating the row-to-domain mapping already in the private bin() helper.
